original_question: Derive non-trivial bounds for bipartite distinct-distance problems in R^d for d >= 3.
target_in_paper: Section 5, Problem 21 in the current arXiv survey version: the higher-dimensional bipartite open problem asking for non-trivial bounds for bipartite distinct-distances problems in R^d for d >= 3. The nearby Section 5 context defines the bipartite setup by counting only distances between pairs from two sets, via D(P,Q). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation: it correctly identifies that the target is a bipartite distinct-distances problem, that the ambient space is R^d, that the dimension range is d >= 3, and that the goal is to obtain non-trivial bounds rather than an exact asymptotic formula. This matches Section 5, Problem 21 almost verbatim. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
missing_details: The draft does not define what a bipartite distinct-distances problem means in the paper: one has two finite point sets P and Q, and only distances between pairs (p,q) in P x Q are counted; distances within P or within Q are ignored. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))

The draft does not make explicit the operator D(P,Q) used in the surrounding context, namely the number of distinct Euclidean distances ||p-q|| with p in P and q in Q. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))

The paper’s higher-dimensional target is intentionally open-ended: unlike earlier planar bipartite problems in the same section, the paper does not introduce a specific extremal function of m and n here, and explicitly says it is ending the section with a deliberately vague problem because the main higher-dimensional difficulties are not yet clear. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))

The draft does not say that no additional structural hypotheses are part of the formal target statement: there are no fixed cardinality parameters, no asymmetry assumptions, and no specified restrictions such as lines, surfaces, parallelism, orthogonality, or sphere/plane exceptions in the formal statement of Problem 21 itself. Those appear only as motivating examples in the preceding higher-dimensional discussion. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))

The refined standalone version should therefore add only the bipartite-distance definition and the Euclidean ambient setting, while avoiding invented extra quantifiers or a broader extremal framework not stated in the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
refined_question: Let P,Q be finite subsets of R^d with d >= 3, and let D(P,Q) = |{||p-q|| : p in P, q in Q}|, where only distances between one point of P and one point of Q are counted. Derive non-trivial bounds for higher-dimensional bipartite distinct-distances problems in R^d; equivalently, obtain non-trivial upper and/or lower bounds for D(P,Q) in this bipartite setting. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
justification: The draft clearly targets the higher-dimensional continuation of the bipartite-distances discussion in Section 5, not any earlier planar or non-bipartite problem. Section 5 first defines the bipartite distance-counting convention and D(P,Q), then its “Higher dimensions” paragraph notes some partial higher-dimensional examples and concludes with Problem 21, stated as a deliberately vague request for non-trivial bounds in R^d for d >= 3. Because the official target is itself deliberately non-specific, the most paper-faithful refinement is to keep that scope and add only the missing formal definition of the bipartite distance count, without inventing a named extremal quantity or extra hypotheses. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
